subject: Milestone Acceptance + Price Safeguards for Acme MAP
body:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acmeretail.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed MAP milestones + pricing guardrails

Samantha — great conversation this morning. Attached is a first draft of the mutual action plan (MAP-Acme-Nov2026.xlsx) that aligns the evaluation milestones to the commercial milestones we discussed. Key asks:

- Pilot evaluation (2 weeks): 100k inference tokens / day simulated load test.
- P0 success metric: 95th percentile latency < 220ms and model quality pass rate >= 92% on their eval set.
- Ramp schedule after pilot: commit to a 6-month phased ramp (month 1: 25% expected spend of committed baseline, month 3: 60%, month 6: 100%).
- Proposed committed baseline: 2M inference tokens / month (discounted unit price enclosed).

Two commercial items I want to flag up front so we can avoid surprises during contracting:
1) True-up cadence and calculation: we propose monthly true-ups against committed baseline with a +30 day grace for usage spikes.
2) Price protection: lock listed unit price for 12 months from signature unless the parties mutually agree to changes.

Can you confirm those milestones look right and flag any internal procurement/legal concerns? If those are okay I’ll loop in Neha and David to pre-empt redlines.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

---

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmeretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acmeretail.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP milestones + pricing guardrails

Jordan — thanks for the MAP. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/legal here before we proceed to terms:

1) True-up: procurement prefers quarterly true-ups rather than monthly, with a pro-rata billing model. Monthly reconciliations increase our AP overhead. Would Redwood consider quarterly true-ups for the first 12 months?
2) Price protection: Acme needs a protection if Redwood increases list prices for comparable customers — we’d request a clause that caps increases at CPI + 3% or allows Acme to terminate with 60 days notice if increases exceed that cap.
3) Definition of billable usage: we need clarity on what counts as billable tokens — specifically whether cached prefix tokens, system prompts, or embeddings for search are included. Our legal want those defined to avoid surprise spikes.

I’ve attached a short note from our procurement team (pdf) outlining the preferred true-up cadence and a draft redline they usually push. Happy to jump on a call.

—Samantha
Samantha Cole
VP, Digital Platforms — Acme Retail

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmeretail.com>, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:36:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed MAP milestones + pricing guardrails — procurement asks

Neha / David — forwarding Samantha’s procurement note. Procurement asks for: quarterly true-ups, a price increase cap tied to CPI + 3%, and precise definition of billable usage (cache/system prompts/embeddings).

My recommendation:
- Accept quarterly true-ups for the first 12 months of a pilot + 90-day billing lag, then revert to monthly for the committed term. This addresses AP concerns and keeps Redwood protected for long-term economics.
- Counter on price protection: offer price lock for 12 months from signature and a cap on increases after that equal to CPI + 4% (Redwood needs some headroom). Include termination right for Acme if increase > CPI + 8% (negotiation lever).
- Define billable usage as: all tokens consumed for inference responses and system prompts, minus server-side prefix cache hits (we will not bill tokens served from cache), and embeddings billed separately with defined unit.

Neha — can Legal prepare a short clause set capturing the above? David — can you confirm the feasibility of excluding prefix cache hits from billing and how we’d instrument usage exports for quarterly reconciliation?

Jordan

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Proposed MAP milestones + pricing guardrails — procurement asks

Samantha / Jordan — thanks. I reviewed the procurement points and prepared a redline (attached: Redlines-Acme-TrackChanges.pdf). High-level positions:

- True-up cadence: we will accept quarterly true-ups for the pilot (first 12 months) with a reconciliation statement due 30 days after quarter end and payment due 60 days after statement. For committed term, revert to monthly true-ups as Jordan suggested.
- Price protection: we will provide a 12-month fixed price. After 12 months, price changes capped at CPI + 4% for the following 12 months. If increases exceed CPI + 8% in any 12-month period, Acme may terminate with 60 days’ notice and receive a pro-rata credit for pre-paid committed capacity.
- Billable usage definition: add explicit language — billable tokens = request tokens + response tokens + system tokens; prefix cache hits, autocomplete suggestions served from client-side cache, and tokens used solely for internal monitoring are excluded. Embeddings and search vectors billed under a separate line item with unit and rounding rules.

I redlined the contract to include audit rights (read-only) for usage exports and a reconciliation data package (CSV with token counts, cache-hit indicators) to be delivered on the reconciliation schedule. That should be acceptable to procurement.

David — we’ll need a short technical appendix (one page) describing the usage export schema. Jordan — I can attach the redline to the HubSpot deal or send a DocuSign envelope once we have Acme sign-off on the MAP.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmeretail.com>, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP milestones + pricing guardrails — proposal from Redwood

Samantha / Tom — appreciate the quick turn. Based on procurement points and legal positions above, here's a consolidated proposal for Acme to review (attached the MAP + tracked redline):

1) MAP & Ramp: Pilot as-is (2 weeks) then phased ramp to committed baseline (2M tokens / month) over 6 months (25% month 1, 60% month 3, 100% month 6).
2) True-ups & invoicing: Quarterly true-ups for the pilot (12 months) with reconciliation statement due 30 days after quarter end and payment due 60 days after statement. Post-pilot, revert to monthly true-ups for the committed term.
3) Price protection: Price locked for 12 months from signature. After that, changes capped at CPI + 4% for the next 12 months. If increases exceed CPI + 8% in any 12-month period, Acme may terminate with 60 days’ notice and receive pro-rata credit for unused committed capacity.
4) Billable usage: Billable tokens = request + response + system tokens. Exclude server-side prefix cache hits from billing. Embeddings billed separately with the attached unit table. We will provide a usage export CSV and a short technical appendix describing fields for reconciliation.

Next steps: please confirm by EOD Mon 23 Nov if procurement can accept the quarterly true-up for the pilot and the proposed price protection language. If yes, Neha will upload the redline to HubSpot and prepare a DocuSign envelope for signature.

If you’d prefer a quick call to finalize, I’m available Mon 23 (10–12 PT).

Best,
Jordan

[Attachments referenced: MAP-Acme-Nov2026.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redlines-Acme-TrackChanges.pdf (contract redline)]
